English.Char_Desc_2000:
Combine Word Files joins every Word (.docx) file in a folder into one Word file, <folder name>_combined.docx, saved in the same folder. Files are joined in natural page-number order (page 2 before page 10), with a divider line between them. Each file keeps its own fonts, spacing, page size, orientation, margins, pictures, tables, lists, footnotes, endnotes and comments; a file with a different page size or a sideways page starts on a new page. Headers and footers come from the first file. You are asked before an existing combined file is replaced. Microsoft Word is not needed to combine the files, only to open the result.
Before you install: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. The installer is not code-signed (a signing certificate is a paid yearly service), so Windows may show a blue "Windows protected your PC" box: click More info, then Run anyway. A few antivirus programs wrongly flag new unsigned programs; you can check the download against the SHA-256 fingerprint on its release page. No administrator password is needed.

Permissions.Distribution_Permissions: Combine Word Files is free to use and share. Download sites may list it and offer the unchanged Setup.exe, or link to the download page.
Permissions.EULA: Combine Word Files is free and comes with no warranty. Use it at your own risk. The free parts it is built from keep their own licenses, listed in the licenses folder it installs.
